How much does it cost to run a computer monitor?

A typical computer monitor uses about 30 watts (15–80W depending on the model). Used for 6 hours per day, 5 days a week, it costs about 4.7p per day and £12.32 a year at the current price cap rate.

Cost per day
4.7p
About £12.32 a year at 6 hours per day, 5 days a week.

Standing charge not included.

Adjust for yours
Ofgem price cap average for 1 Oct – 31 Dec 2026 (standard variable tariff, Direct Debit, England, Scotland & Wales).

About these figures

Source for the typical figure: Typical range (estimate). See how we calculate.

Ways to cut the cost

  • Switch off at the wall rather than leaving devices on standby.
  • Turn down screen brightness; it's often the biggest single draw on a TV.
  • Use power-saving or eco modes on consoles and computers.

Questions

How much does it cost to run a computer monitor per hour?

At 26.32p/kWh, a 30W model costs about 0.8p an hour while it's running.

How much does it cost to run a computer monitor per year?

About £12.32 a year, based on 6 hours per day, 5 days a week. Change the sliders above to match how you use yours.

Is the standing charge included?

No. You pay the standing charge every day whether or not the appliance is used, so it isn't part of the cost of running it.

How do I find my computer monitor's actual power use?

Check the rating label, plug or manual for the wattage, or the energy label for kWh figures. A plug-in energy monitor shows exactly what it uses.
